notes: Cinderlea's ash roads (docs/WORLD_LIFE_ROADS.md), owned by the Cinderlea region agent. Few travel here, and those who do are kind and quiet about it: the Order walking a pilgrim south, a pilgrim coming back who should not have, a scavenger with a pack of bronze, the Order's carts. The rest is the unquiet: wights who still wave, a fallen knight who still salutes, choristers holding the note over a bend, a bell-bearer walking a round nobody gave it.

talk.say: Candles, bread and bandages. What else does a pilgrim need, going up there?
Nothing on this road wants your purse. That's the worry.

consequence.notice: The sutler will tell Pilgrim's Ash who set on him.
consequence.killing_notice: The sutler's guard is dead on the ash road.

rescue.say: The ash gives them up at dusk. You kept them off us -- here.

name: Wights under the ash
notes: The un-ended people of Greyfold lying in the ash by the road; with the waving tell one of them stands in the road and waves, the way they still do, and whoever waves back is among them.

name: A fallen knight on the road
notes: One of the Order's knights gone wrong, standing a vigil at a bend in the dark. He salutes before he swings; the form is all that is left.

lines.speaker: A Tolling knight
lines.spring: *(He salutes, and gives ground the one step the form allows, and comes on.)*

name: Choristers holding the note
notes: Two choristers stand either side of a bend at dusk with their mouths open and hold the note across the road; silence stops them.

lines.speaker: A chorister
lines.spring: *(The note arrives before the voice does, as a pressure in the chest.)*

name: A bell-bearer walking its round
notes: A bell-bearer walking a round across the road and back, ringing at nothing; nobody gave it the round.

name: The Order walking a pilgrim south
notes: Two knights of the Tolling Order walking a pilgrim to the line, the Vigil Book's third rule: talking about the weather, so that the last thing the pilgrim hears is a voice saying something ordinary.

talk.say: We are walking her to the ring. Walk a way with us, if you're going south; talk about the eels, or the weather. Don't make a speech. — There's a place off the road the pilgrims stop at before the Choir, if you've not seen it.

hook.rumour: The knight says the pilgrims stop at {place} on the way south.

talk.say: It's a fine day for it, isn't it? Grey, but fine. — No, I'm not frightened. I was, at the ninth waystone. I sat on it a while. Then I wasn't.

name: A pilgrim who turned back
notes: A pilgrim coming back up the road from the Choir, which the Order has no rule for, sitting at the roadside not knowing the way back, because nobody writes it down.

talk.say: I got as far as the ring and I couldn't. I don't know the way back; nobody writes the way back down. Would you walk me to {place}? I'll not be any trouble. I've stopped being any trouble.
talk.thanks: There's a roof. — They'll give me bread there, and my name back, and not ask. Thank you. Here: it's the coin I was going to leave on the Tenth.

name: A scavenger of the Ring
notes: One of Coll Brisket's scavengers walking the Ashgrid road with a pack of Builders' bronze; knows where the dead city has been opened lately.

talk.say: Bronze for the Tallymen, four a pound if it's clean, which it never is. — If you're digging, don't dig where it's quiet. There's a roof opened up off the road where it's never been quiet at all.

hook.rumour: The scavenger says the dead city has been opened at {place}.

name: The ninth-day cart to Greyfold
notes: The Order's handcart, taking the ninth-day basket of ash-cakes from Pilgrim's Ash out to Greyfold, where Nan Greyfold lays the tables; a knight between the shafts and a novice walking beside.

talk.say: Ash-cakes for Greyfold, candles for the Choir, bread for anyone. The Order doesn't sell. It'll take a coin, though, if you leave one; it goes on the Tenth.
I count the wights we pass. Nineteen this morning. They waved.

consequence.notice: You struck at the Order's cart. Pilgrim's Ash will hear it before you get there.
consequence.killing_notice: The Order's carter is dead on the Greyfold road, and the basket for the tables with him.

rescue.say: They came up out of the ash at the cart like it was a table. — Thank you. Take a cake. They're for the dead, but the dead won't mind.

name: The Wardens' chalk train
notes: A Wardens' packhorse carrying chalk from the West Walk to bank the fires on the grey side and set the Greyline stones, with a Warden at its head.

talk.say: Chalk for the fires, and whatever else the Rest has sent. It's all for sale except the chalk.
Every fire on the grey side is banked with Vale chalk, so that when a patrol turns back the last thing it sees is white. This year some of it has come back grey.

consequence.notice: You struck a Warden on the West Walk road. The Roll will have your name by morning.
consequence.killing_notice: A Warden is dead on the West Walk road.

rescue.say: Put down, then. Twice this month on this stretch. — The Rest pays for that.
